subject.title: [Bug]: Bootstrap files in agentDir are silently ignored — only workspace directory files are injected into system prompt

question: Should OpenClaw treat configured agentDir as a trusted bootstrap prompt source, or keep agentDir runtime-state-only and warn when bootstrap files are misplaced there?
rationale: Current code and docs separate workspace prompt context from agentDir runtime/auth state, while the linked PRs propose incompatible policies; this changes the security and upgrade contract rather than only a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Keep agentDir state-only and warn
options.body: Land the warning/docs/doctor direction so users get an actionable diagnostic while prompt instructions remain workspace-owned.

options.title: Load explicit agentDir bootstrap files
options.body: Adopt an agentDir merge/override PR, but require clear trust-boundary docs, fresh-install and upgrade proof, and tests across all bootstrap callers.

options.title: Defer and close linked PRs
options.body: If maintainers do not want either behavior now, close the implementation PRs and leave a clear documented workaround using per-agent workspace paths.

recommendation.title: Keep agentDir state-only and warn
recommendation.body: Land the warning/docs/doctor direction so users get an actionable diagnostic while prompt instructions remain workspace-owned.

likelyOwner.reason: The central bootstrap resolver history and current code ownership trail point most strongly to steipete for the workspace versus agentDir prompt-source decision.
